<!-- docs-drift-check -->
### 📓 Docs Drift Check
This PR changes **1** package(s): `@objectstack/runtime`, touching **17** documentable anchor(s).

**6** hand-written doc(s) NAME something this change touched and may need an implementation-accuracy re-verification:

- `content/docs/api/error-catalog.mdx`  _(via invalid_value (literal, a string literal in actionSelectionIdsOrRefuse), max_items (literal, a string literal in actionSelectionIdsOrRefuse))_
- `content/docs/api/plugin-endpoints.mdx`  _(via invalid_value (literal, a string literal in actionSelectionIdsOrRefuse))_
- `content/docs/automation/flows.mdx`  _(via invalid_value (literal, a string literal in actionSelectionIdsOrRefuse))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/field-types.mdx`  _(via invalid_value (literal, a string literal in actionSelectionIdsOrRefuse))_
- `content/docs/data-modeling/validation-rules.mdx`  _(via invalid_value (literal, a string literal in actionSelectionIdsOrRefuse))_
- `content/docs/permissions/system-context.mdx`  _(via actionSelectionIsRead (symbol, a top-level function), invalid_value (literal, a string literal in actionSelectionIdsOrRefuse))_

⛔ **1** release-owned page(s) also name something this change touched. These are **read-only**:

- `content/docs/releases/v18/18-2.mdx`  _(via invalid_value (literal, a string literal in actionSelectionIdsOrRefuse))_

> `content/docs/releases/` is RELEASE-OWNED (AGENTS.md "Documentation Guardrails"): release
> notes are written centrally at release time, and a code PR that edits them is the exact PR
> that guardrail exists to stop. They are still audited — read-only. If one of them is actually
> wrong, **file an issue** or open a dedicated docs-only PR; do not edit it here.

<details><summary>What this run could not see</summary>

- **3** name(s) were too generic to anchor anything (single lowercase words)
- the SDK route bridge reached **67** of **249** client-bound route-ledger rows — the other **182** have no registrar `path:` tail to select them, so pages documenting THEIR client methods cannot appear above, on this or any run. Of those **182**: **0** are remediable by widening that discovery convention (an in-repo file declares the path; the convention did not scan it); **59** are structural — on a ledger where NOT ONE row is declared in-repo, so no discovery change reaches them at any price; **123** are undecided (no in-repo declaration, on a ledger that has other in-repo registrars — absence and an unreadable spelling are not distinguishable here). The rows themselves: `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --bridge-coverage`
- a page that states a rule by its **inputs** shares no identifier with the **emitter** that implements the rule, so an emitter-only diff cannot list it — not on this run and not on any run. Measured on #11430: `content/docs/protocol/objectql/types.mdx` documents the text-family column mapping by the ObjectQL type names it maps FROM (`text` / `textarea` / `html`) while the diff changed `createColumn`; it went unlisted, and it was the page that diff falsified, in four places. No shared token exists to detect this on, so a rule your change carries has to be re-read by hand in the pages that restate it.
- a key NAME is not a key, so the hand re-read the line above prescribes can land on the wrong schema. The same spelling is authorable on one governed type and a `[REMOVED]` tombstone on another for each of `active`, `aria`, `joins`, `objects`, `template`, `tools` and `version` (censused on #19093 over the liveness ledger's governed types, top-level keys); nothing in a search result distinguishes the two, so a grep hit on a LIVE example reads as evidence about the DEAD key. Measured on #19059: `content/docs/ai/agents.mdx` was reported as contradicting the `agent.tools` tombstone over its `tools:` example at `:161`, which is inside the `defineSkill({` block opened at `:155` — the page was already correct. Settle ownership by PARSING the value against both schemas, never by the name: that literal PASSES `SkillSchema`, and as an `AgentSchema` it FAILS at `tools` with the tombstone prescription. ⛔ These names are not the whole class — a key retired through a `.strict()` guidance map leaves no tombstone in the walked shape and none of them here (`tool.category`, live as `AIToolDefinition.category`).

Coarse fallback — **30** page(s) merely *mention* a changed package (the pre-#9192 predicate, kept for the deliberately-wide backstop): `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 28ba01fe6939ac40a5e72efe32ea6b7680eed33e` → `packageMentionDocs`.
</details>

<details><summary>Which tree this was computed on</summary>

This run read `content/docs` from `f40567668c35f6a3c72a3af03757686099a46beb` — the merge of head `59428ccd16bec2ea7cb9d45d4f63bd6ec9edf1ec` into base `28ba01fe6939ac40a5e72efe32ea6b7680eed33e`, which is what `actions/checkout` gives a `pull_request` run. **Not** the PR head.

A worktree cut from an older `main` holds a different `content/docs`, so re-deriving there can legitimately return a different list — that is a **different tree, not a wrong row**. To answer on the same tree:

```sh
# while this PR is open — GitHub drops the merge commit once it closes
git fetch origin f40567668c35f6a3c72a3af03757686099a46beb && git checkout f40567668c35f6a3c72a3af03757686099a46beb
# afterwards, rebuild it from the two parents, which stay fetchable
git fetch origin 28ba01fe6939ac40a5e72efe32ea6b7680eed33e 59428ccd16bec2ea7cb9d45d4f63bd6ec9edf1ec && git checkout -B drift-repro 28ba01fe6939ac40a5e72efe32ea6b7680eed33e && git merge --no-ff 59428ccd16bec2ea7cb9d45d4f63bd6ec9edf1ec

node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs --json 28ba01fe6939ac40a5e72efe32ea6b7680eed33e
```

⚠️ That checkout carried **uncommitted changes**, so the commit above does not fully identify what was read.
</details>

> Advisory only, and a **precision-first** one (#9192): a page is listed because it names a
> symbol, wire route or SDK method this diff touched — not because it mentions a changed
> package. Each row says which anchor put it there, so a wrong row is reportable rather than
> merely annoying. To re-verify, run the `docs-accuracy-audit` workflow scoped to these files:
> `node scripts/docs-audit/affected-docs.mjs 28ba01fe6939ac40a5e72efe32ea6b7680eed33e` → pass the list as
> `args.docs`, on the commit named under **Which tree this was computed on**.

**Contract-tier review (L2) and adversarial read — REWORK · head `9abda326b5b2bf07ae4602c8ac26b74c18fe8622`.** The reviewer was an isolated `CONTRACT_REVIEW_TIER` thread, read-only. It ran the PR's own pins (65 passed) and its own real-stack probes from a `git archive` export. The PR merges cleanly into `origin/main`.

**Holds.**
- The narrowing is the order's steps 1–5 and 7, plus seat ruling A.
- Both declarations are true; no new error code.
- The exemptions are exactly the declarative update, `type: 'api'` and the system principal.
- REST, MCP and the host share one sequence.
- The verdict is consumed before the AI hand-off and again on re-admission.
- Chunk boundaries, throws, empty, null and duplicates behave as documented.
- Public title, body, commits and changeset are rule-level.

**Owed in this PR, before the seat's delta read:**
1. `content/docs/ui/actions.mdx` (~669-671): the sentence says more than the door reads. The ids are read as rows of the object the call names. Scope the sentence to that, or make it true.
2. The selection read asks the same operation the per-record door asks for its record (`get`, not `list`), so a selection the caller can read record by record is not refused whole. Pin it. If it cannot, the changeset's FROM/TO states the difference and the caller's fix.
3. Test titles in `action-selection-caller-scope.pin.test.ts` (~272, ~306, ~321-322 and header item 3): state the rule only. Name no session condition.
4. Nits:
   - the changeset and docs list every near-miss spelling refused (four, not three);
   - re-attach `laxActionParams`' docblock;
   - the app-todo action's AI description no longer says "one bulk operation".

**Not in this PR (with the security seat):** two adjacent items found at the doors, on code this PR does not change; and whether ids are handed on as sent or normalised.
